Vijasan Caves, also known as Vijasan Monastery, are a group of Buddhist caves located in the Bhaja village near Lonavala in Maharashtra, India. These caves date back to the 2nd century BC and are believed to have been excavated during the Satavahana dynasty. The caves are situated on a hillside and consist of around 22 rock-cut caves.

The Vijasan Caves are notable for their unique architecture and intricate carvings, including sculptures of various Hindu and Buddhist deities such as Shiva and Buddha. The caves also contain inscriptions in Brahmi script and Pali language, providing valuable historical insights into the period when they were created.

These caves are considered an important pilgrimage site for Buddhists and attract visitors from around the world who come to admire the religious significance and artistic beauty of the site. The Vijasan Caves are part of the larger group of Buddhist caves in the region, including the famous Karla Caves and Bhaja Caves.

Overall, the Vijasan Caves are a significant archaeological site that showcases the rich cultural heritage of ancient India and serves as a reminder of the country's deep-rooted Buddhist tradition.
